facts.detail: The final statement was published on 17 March 2026.
The regulatory decisions apply from April 2026 to March 2031.
The review covers fixed telecoms markets underpinning broadband, mobile and business connections.
The decisions are intended to promote competition and investment in gigabit-capable networks.

guard_streams.write_limit: A regulatory objective and review period do not establish current serviceability at a parcel.

facts.detail: The TAR framework covers physical infrastructure, wholesale local access, leased-lines access and inter-exchange connectivity.
The statement publishes a dedicated volume on non-pricing remedies.
The statement publishes a dedicated volume on pricing remedies.
The statement includes a quality-of-service volume and legal direction.

guard_streams.write_limit: Wholesale market remedies and quality directions are not premises-level coverage records.

facts.detail: The supporting documents include WLA postcode-sector classifications.
The supporting documents include LLA postcode-sector classifications.
A separate schedule classifies postcode sectors for dark-fibre access.
Inter-exchange connectivity is represented through an exchange-classification schedule.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regulatory postcode-sector and exchange classifications cannot be joined as exact parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The TAR hub was updated on 28 July 2026.
The July update links a consultation on Openreach commercial offers notified in June 2026.
A June 2026 Call for Inputs preceded the consultation.
The hub records May 2026 modifications to SMP conditions.

guard_streams.write_limit: A current regulatory update is not a current network-build or address-availability update.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Openreach proposed commercial offers consultation

facts.detail: The consultation was published on 28 July 2026.
The consultation closes at 5pm on 27 August 2026.
Ofcom's views on the offers are provisional pending consultation.
Ofcom proposes withdrawal of the Incremental New to Openreach Customer Offer but not intervention on the other notified offers.

guard_streams.write_limit: A proposed regulatory intervention must not be represented as a final decision or parcel-coverage change.

facts.detail: The incremental offer could discount up to £9.50 per qualifying customer for up to 30 months.
A geographic offer provides a one-off £50 discount in specified competitive areas.
The Frontbook ARPU Share Offer would cap average ISP payment for new higher-speed connections at £19.32 per month.
Openreach must give advance notice of certain commercial offers because it has significant market power.

guard_streams.write_limit: Wholesale discounts and notification duties are commercial evidence, not exact availability, price or speed for an end-user parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom provisionally considers the targeted incremental charges not fair and reasonable and potentially harmful to network competition.
Ofcom states wholesale network competition remains under development in most of the UK.
Ofcom notes around half of households able to access full fibre have not yet taken it up.
The other notified offers were provisionally assessed as not warranting intervention.

guard_streams.write_limit: Competition and take-up observations cannot identify which parcel is covered or connected.

facts.detail: Copper retirement is the eventual decommissioning of Openreach's legacy copper network after migration.
Customers may migrate to Openreach FTTP or rival networks.
Ofcom retained a three-stage exchange-by-exchange regulatory framework.
The second-threshold consultation closed and remains pending a final statement.

guard_streams.write_limit: Copper retirement planning does not prove that any specific premises has migrated or can order FTTP.

facts.detail: The second threshold requires ultrafast coverage to 100% of premises in an exchange area, excluding premises directed by Ofcom.
Required notice periods must also be met.
After the threshold, copper charge control can be disapplied at premises where FTTP is available.
Ofcom stated an intention to publish final decisions in autumn 2026.

guard_streams.write_limit: An exchange threshold and regulatory charge-control effect are not accepted parcel-level FTTP evidence.

facts.detail: The complaints update was published on 23 July 2026.
The latest figures cover January to March 2026.
Major-provider broadband complaints reached six per 100,000 customers.
Ofcom described this as an all-time low compared with a 2011 peak of 40 per 100,000.

guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly complaint rates are provider-level service-quality indicators, not parcel availability or measured speed.

facts.detail: TalkTalk generated the most fixed-broadband complaints in the quarter.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints.
Major complaint drivers included faults, service and provisioning, complaint handling, billing, pricing and charges.
Ofcom says it cannot act on individual complaints and uses the data to identify sector trends and possible systemic issues.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider rankings and complaint reasons must not change an individual parcel's confidence score.

facts.detail: The May table reports 837,340 contracted premises.
The May table reports 256,680 built contracted premises.
A footnote records 420 premises removed from Bedfordshire, Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes for later re-addition.
A footnote records 2,140 North Shropshire premises removed for later re-addition.

guard_streams.write_limit: Administrative removals and later re-additions show that monthly contract tables can be revised and are not immutable parcel evidence.

facts.detail: The July table reports 838,490 contracted premises.
The July table reports 287,510 built contracted premises.
The Cheshire row reports 18,460 contracted and zero built premises.
Central Cornwall reports 6,940 contracted and 6,940 built contracted premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded contract-level progress cannot identify address readiness, orderability or current coverage.

facts.detail: The GBVS collection was last updated on 16 March 2026.
The collection links GBVS Beneficiary Terms and Conditions version 10.1.
The collection links GBVS Supplier Terms and Conditions version 10.1.
The March 2026 update added a link to the Gigabit Broadband Availability Checker.

guard_streams.write_limit: A terms version or checker link is not proof that a voucher was awarded or a network was delivered.

facts.detail: GBVS focuses on local projects where no Project Gigabit procurement or contract, existing coverage or planned commercial coverage applies.
Eligible premises may receive vouchers worth up to £4,500 toward installation.
Canonical continuation and runtime records show no live owner and no active or over-15-minute PENDING execution.
No parcel candidate, measured-speed row or accuracy promotion is permitted until accepted r2 bytes, exact join and postjoin readback exist.
